messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT: High 5xx rate & connection drops on eu-central (detected by slo-monitor). Paging oncall group. Pager: https://pager.redwood/INC-5621 :rotating_light:
ria: seen it, jumping on. I can see a traffic dip and spikes in 5xx around 12:14 UTC.
matt: on my way, what do we know about upstream provider? any ongoing deployments?
danielle: no deploys scheduled. Provider status shows partial packet loss in eu-central-2 for provider-a (as of 12:12).
ria: running quick query on router metrics: `sum(rate(http_requests_total{region="eu-central"} [1m])) by (provider,route)`
ria: logs show TTL errors and aborted connections to provider-a nodes. Also a sentinel of increased queue_rejects.
infra-bot: provider-a-eucentral-2: degraded network (packet-loss 6%). See https://status.provider-a.example/incident/1298
matt: ok, plan: we need immediate mitigation to keep customer traffic alive. Options: reroute to provider-b, start regional drain from eu-central to fallback region, or apply soft brownout for best-effort features. Thoughts?
danielle: provider-b capacity ok but latency +30ms for a lot of EU customers. We should prefer routing critical traffic to other regions/providers and downgrade bulk background requests.
sophie: support: a few large customers already filed error alerts. Suggest we prioritize Enterprise traffic with SLA.
ria: agree. Action items I'm going to do now: 1) enable provider failover policy for eu-central to prefer provider-b; 2) apply token-level rate limit increase to dedicated customers only; 3) partial brownout of non-critical features (vector-ops, batch-embeddings) for free-tier. Posting commands now.
ria: runbook step: `infractl traffic-policy apply --region eu-central --policy provider-b-prefer --dry-run=false`
ria: running...
inc-bot: ACTION: traffic policy change initiated by ria at 12:18 UTC.
infra-bot: policy apply returned: 202 ACCEPTED, change in steady state expected ~30s.
matt: while that's rolling, can we throttle incoming open streaming sessions from free-tier to cut concurrent connections?
danielle: yes. I'll update the quota service: `kubectl exec -c api quota-ctrl -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/admin/rate-limit -d '{"tier":"free","concurrent":50}'`
sophie: I'll draft a customer note for the impacted large customers (we'll include estimated mitigation and ETA).
ria: started canary failover route. Monitoring traces for error rate drop.
aria: (typo) ignore
matt: error_rate eu-central provider-a: 4xx stable, 5xx down from 12% -> 7% after 45s. Good trend. But we're seeing oscillation: some traffic keeps hitting provider-a nodes that haven't fully drained.
danielle: I see backend drain still in progress. There might be stuck connections. I'll trigger a graceful drain on provider-a nodes in eu-central: `infractl node drain --provider provider-a --region eu-central --grace 30s`
infra-bot: drain job queued: job_id=drain-834. Estimated finish 2m.
support-bot: Notifying customers with >1k qps: #customer-updates channel and email templates queued.
sophie: sent initial DM to 3 enterprise POCs with advisory and ETA 20m.
matt: we need a fallback if drain doesn't finish: do a regional failover to eu-west as a last resort. Can infra take that?
danielle: capacity in eu-west is 60% used but can take redirected traffic if we cut some of the background work and tighten batch windows.
ria: initiating partial brownout: disable experimental realtime-sync feature for non-enterprise tokens: `featurectl toggle realtime-sync --region eu-central --off --selector "!tier:enterprise"`
inc-bot: FEATURE_TOGGLE: realtime-sync disabled for non-enterprise in eu-central by ria at 12:22 UTC.
ria: monitoring: 5xx now at 3.1% and connection drops trending down. Some clients still seeing retry storms — recommend increasing upstream retry-jitter to prevent stampedes.
matt: increasing retry jitter on edge: `yaml apply` snippet below:
```
edge-routes:
  retry_policy:
    attempts: 3
    per_try_timeout: 2s
    jitter: 0.5
```
danielle: done. Also raising rate limit for dedicated tiers to prevent throttles: `quota admin set --tier dedicated --burst 2000`
sophie: customers on free tier will see reduced throughput for batch jobs — included explanation in the note.
ria: handoff: @oncall-ops, you're now owning mitigation for steady-state monitoring and customer comms. I'll stay for escalation if drain fails.
oncall-ops: taking over. I'll monitor for 30m and if 5xx > 2% we'll trigger regional failover to eu-west and inform PG.
matt: create ticket for post-incident RCA: link: https://issues.redwood/INC-5621-RCA. Assign to infra and runtime teams.
ria: adding immediate hypothesis: provider-a network degradation -> partial node isolation -> stuck connections -> incomplete drain -> oscillation. Next: collect tcpdump from affected nodes and provider logs.
danielle: collected pcaps and forwarded to provider support. Also opening support ticket with provider-a case #PA-9812.
infra-bot: PROV_CASE: provider-a ticket opened PA-9812 by danielle at 12:30 UTC.
sophie: customer comms updated with PA ticket and mitigation steps.
oncall-ops: steady-state checks: latency +18ms in failover paths, 5xx at 1.8% now. Will keep throttles and brownout for 45 minutes unless we see regressions.
ria: thanks team. After action: schedule canary to re-enable realtime-sync for non-enterprise once 5xx < 0.5% for 15m.
matt: agree. Also add automated rollback thresholds to the traffic policy to prevent oscillation in future (e.g., require error rate <1% for 2m before switching back to provider-a).
danielle: noted, I'll add to infra backlog and PR a guard clause.
sophie: closing loop with support — sent final advisory to impacted customers and updated docs.
inc-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): Recorded by oncall-ops at 12:40 UTC. Postmortem required.
ria: creating initial incident summary for RCA and tagging postmortem owners.
oncall-ops: leaving monitors in place; handoff to day shift @matt for follow-ups.
matt: +1. We'll run the RCA tomorrow 14:00 UTC.
support-bot: notifications: all affected customers emailed.
ria: thanks all.
